newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin vows Chechen peace process to go on.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin vows Chechen peace process to go on.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Thursday the Chechen peace process would continue despite the sacking of security chief Alexander Lebed, architect of a fragile truce in the breakaway region.
"I believe the peace process (in Chechnya) will continue as before...One man cannot change how such an important matter is handled," he told Russian television.
Chernomyrdin said a joint commission was currently working in Chechnya on how to implement the August 31 peace deal which Lebed put together.
"The information available to me suggests that negotiations are proceeding constructively," he added.
President Boris Yeltsin went on national television to announce he was firing Lebed for what he called his lack of team spirit and open ambition to become Russia's next leader.

Lebed's peace accord with the Chechen separatists brought a halt to a bloody 21-month conflict in which tens of thousands of people, mainly civilians, died. Some of Lebed's political rivals say the deal is a betrayal of Russian national interests.
